## How to read it

- **Status** `queued` (approved, no lane has started), `porting` (a lane is working), `review` (its completion checklist is met and it awaits a reviewer), `done` (accepted).
  A row moves one stage at a time; `node scripts/ports.mjs set-status <id> <status>` updates `ports.json` and this file together.
- **Pinned commit** is the upstream revision the port is measured against. A Package that exists must carry the same pin and license in its `provenance.json`; the gate checks it.
  A queued row is pinned when it is listed (the commit of the latest npm release when the registry records one, else the default branch head); the lane confirms or re-pins before it starts.
- **Kind** `port` translates an upstream program; `adapter` is original code on an upstream SDK or protocol; `move` brings existing code in from another repository; `original` is new work.
- **Lane** is the port lane (the port branch `<lane>`); for a queued row it is the name the lane will take.
- To port a row, give the [porting Skill](../components/extension-port/skills/pigpen-pi-extension-port/SKILL.md) its id: `port row <id>`.

## Queue order

1. `rpiv-todo`: Model-facing todo list shown as a live overlay that survives reload and compaction.
2. `rpiv-ask-user-question`: Structured multi-question questionnaire the model calls instead of guessing, with an RPC fallback and locales.
3. `plannotator`: Plan mode with a browser review UI, code and PR diff review, and annotate-last-message. The flagship demo.
4. `ponytail`: The "lazy senior dev" mode: /ponytail modes, review, audit, gain and debt commands, plus six skills.
5. `langfuse-observability`: Traces prompts, turns, generations and tool calls to Langfuse. Opt-in; prompts leave the machine.

## Details

### `extension-porter`: Extension porter (pig-porter, pig-extension-porter)

- Kind: move. The strict porting Skill, the equivalence harness (pigeq) and the two Piglets that carry them. This is the workflow every other row is ported with.
- Upstream path: `piglets/porter/skills/pig-porter` in PiG
- Notes: Reviewed (ACCEPT-WITH-FIXES). Lane pigpen-porter-driver keeps tuning the Skill and harness from every port below. Reviewed and merged for the first release.

### `dirty-repo-guard`: dirty-repo-guard

- Kind: port. Pi example extension that refuses a session switch or fork while the git tree is dirty. The first port made with the porter.
- Upstream path: `packages/coding-agent/examples/extensions/dirty-repo-guard.ts` in Pi
- Notes: 11/11 scenarios identical to Pi, 17/17 mutations killed.

### `herdr`: herdr agent-state reporter

- Kind: original. Reports PiG idle, working and blocked to herdr through its documented pane report-agent contract.
- Notes: Go port on the public SDK (it replaced the earlier Node extension). Reviewed and merged for the first release.

### `web-search`: Web search and fetch (pi-web-access)

- Kind: port. Search, fetch, retain sources and retrieve bounded content: providers, routing, cache, extraction. Delivered in reviewed slices.
- Notes: npm 483,117 in 30 days, 1,562 stars (2026-09-29). No browser-cookie access by default; no paid fallback without configuration. Reviewed and merged for the first release.

### `acp`: ACP: editors drive a PiG agent (pi-acp)

- Kind: port. stdio Agent Client Protocol adapter over the PiG agent, with declared capability limits. A standalone bridge, not an extension.
- Upstream path: `schema/schema.json` in Agent Client Protocol
- Notes: npm 300,748 in 30 days. Port from the ACP spec, not from pi-acp's unmerged pull requests. Reviewed and merged for the first release.

### `ahp`: AHP: multi-client session host (pi-ahp)

- Kind: port. Host extension serving Microsoft's Agent Host Protocol over WebSocket: reconnect, reconciliation, auth. No listener unless configured.
- Upstream path: `clients/go` in Agent Host Protocol
- Notes: Lowest demand of the protocol rows (1,206 npm downloads in 30 days); the protocol is Microsoft's and VS Code uses it. Reviewed and merged for the first release.

### `a2a`: A2A: serve PiG tasks, call remote agents

- Kind: adapter. Original adapter on a2a-go: an A2A server for PiG tasks and a client for remote agents, interoperating with kagent. Listener off unless configured.
- Notes: No popular Pi A2A extension exists; @bacnh85/pi-a2a is a behaviour reference only. Reviewed and merged for the first release.

### `jev`: Jev: typed judgments and gates (y0usaf/pi-jev)

- Kind: port. Tool-call gate, output judge and jev_ask, with the roadmap's defect corrections. Opt-in; discloses that content leaves the machine.
- Notes: Owner-approved foundation. Small ecosystem (605 npm downloads in 30 days); pi-warden and pi-typesafe are the more installed Jev packages. Reviewed and merged for the first release.

### `typesafe-client`: TypeSafe client (typesafe-sdk-js, system-one-adapter-python)

- Kind: port. Shared Go client for the TypeSafe API, plus a backend that answers the same typed questions with the model PiG is configured with. Used by jev, pi-typesafe and pi-warden.
- Notes: Tests use a fake TypeSafe server; no real API call without an owner-supplied TYPESAFE_API_KEY. The Go contract is committed first so the three extension lanes can build against it. Reviewed and merged for the first release.

### `pi-typesafe`: pi-typesafe (DevMortimer)

- Kind: port. The batched typesafe_evaluate tool and the typed API for extension authors, on the shared Go client. Off by default.
- Notes: npm 7,453 in 30 days (2026-09-29). Depends on the typesafe-client row. Discloses that content goes to the TypeSafe API unless the own-model backend is selected. Reviewed and merged for the first release.

### `pi-warden`: pi-warden (DevMortimer)

- Kind: port. Guardrails that steer instead of interrupt: irreversible calls, off-task calls, stuck loops, unverified done claims. Opt-in, on the shared Go client.
- Notes: npm 7,030 in 30 days, 154 stars (2026-09-29). Depends on the typesafe-client row. A launch-video demo feature; the own-model backend must work. Re-pinned at the warden merge from 0f11867 (the listing-time head) to a12b2703, the commit the port was made against (components/warden/provenance.json); the pi-typesafe upstream is its second one. Reviewed and merged for the first release.

### `pig-play`: pig-play: shared pig sprite and terminal game library

- Kind: move. The canonical pixel pig, palette, half-block rasteriser and terminal game plumbing that every pig game builds on.
- Upstream path: `piglets/standard` in PiG
- Notes: Reviewed and merged for the first release.

### `pig-runner`: PiG Runner

- Kind: move. Obstacle runner starring the pig; starts only on an explicit command.
- Upstream path: `piglets/standard/extensions/pigrunner` in PiG
- Notes: Reviewed and merged for the first release.

### `angry-pigs`: Angry Pigs

- Kind: move. Pig slingshot puzzle game; starts only on an explicit command.
- Upstream path: `piglets/standard/extensions/angrypigs` in PiG
- Notes: Reviewed and merged for the first release.

### `pig-snake`: Pig Snake

- Kind: original. New snake game where every apple adds another pig head, so a herd forms behind the leader. Explicit command only.
- Upstream path: `piglets/standard/extensions/angrypigs` in PiG
- Notes: Sprite access sits behind one interface so it can switch to the shared pig-play library. Reviewed and merged for the first release.

### `session-ingest`: session-ingest (read_session)

- Kind: original. Read another PiG session: turn, tools and stats modes. Moved from the owner's own extensions to the public PiG Go SDK.
- Notes: No popular equivalent exists. Reviewed and merged for the first release.

### `context-info`: context-info (/context, /tools, /cost, /prompts)

- Kind: original. Context, tools, cost and prompt inspection commands with an opt-in footer widget. Moved from the owner's own extensions to the public PiG Go SDK.
- Notes: Moved unless a far more popular Pi extension covers the same job; the lane reports if one does. Reviewed and merged for the first release.

### `skills`: General development Skills (dev-skills)

- Kind: port. Eight general development Skills (tdd, diagnosing-bugs, handoff, research, grilling, prototype, code-review, commit) adapted from public Skills, as one Skills Package. Not in batteries.
- Notes: Names take the pigpen- prefix the Skill gate requires. The adaptations were made from an earlier upstream revision whose commit was not recorded (see the Package CREDITS.md). Reviewed and merged for the first release.

### `rpiv-todo`: rpiv-todo

- Kind: port. Model-facing todo list shown as a live overlay that survives reload and compaction.
- Upstream path: `packages/rpiv-todo` in rpiv-mono
- Notes: npm 200,994 in 30 days. Size S, 3-5 days. The overlay is widget lines (Go SDK stand-in).

### `rpiv-ask-user-question`: rpiv-ask-user-question

- Kind: port. Structured multi-question questionnaire the model calls instead of guessing, with an RPC fallback and locales.
- Upstream path: `packages/rpiv-ask-user-question` in rpiv-mono
- Notes: npm 274,750 in 30 days. Size M, 6-10 days. The owner's Go ask extension is the base. Known gap: pi.events (named skipped tests).

### `plannotator`: Plannotator

- Kind: port. Plan mode with a browser review UI, code and PR diff review, and annotate-last-message. The flagship demo.
- Upstream path: `apps/pi-extension` in plannotator
- Notes: npm 105,444 in 30 days, 9,065 stars (cross-agent). Size L, 15-25 days: net/http plus the embedded prebuilt UI bundle, not a rewrite of the React UI. Start early; version 0.27 churns, so keep the pin.

### `ponytail`: Ponytail

- Kind: port. The "lazy senior dev" mode: /ponytail modes, review, audit, gain and debt commands, plus six skills.
- Notes: npm 69,188 in 30 days, 148,287 stars (marketing signal). Size XS, 1-3 days. Do not repeat the author's own 54% claim as ours.

### `langfuse-observability`: Langfuse observability

- Kind: port. Traces prompts, turns, generations and tool calls to Langfuse. Opt-in; prompts leave the machine.
- Notes: npm 249,668 in 30 days but 11 stars: the count looks partly automated. Size S, 4-7 days. Pairs with LangSmith (@langchain/langsmith-pi-extension) as one observability battery. No default telemetry in batteries.

### `pi-subagents`: pi-subagents (Nico Bailon)
